ratingReasons: The largest gain addresses an important local power connection: the eFuse OUT bypass route falls from 23.026 to 3.174 mm, and CdVdt falls from 11.013 to 5.568 mm while leaving inner1. The protected permission-supply pickup becomes 10.586 mm longer; overall totals already include that collateral cost.

Compensation and LOW gate routes improve by 2.497 and 1.933 mm respectively, and the fan feed saves 8.670 mm. These concrete local changes justify more credit than the modest 0.84% whole-board length reduction alone.

Inner1 signal copper drops by 38.244 mm, and the regenerated native ground BREP gains 22.642 mm² on inner1 and 2.627 mm² on bottom before separate same-net drill subtraction. All 147 ground lands and all 166 main-plane via contacts are preserved.

All 450 connections and frozen functions survive, with genuine JLC/footprint/pad preservation and strong rejected negative controls. Baseline connectivity was already complete, so preservation earns no new performance improvement credit.

The score stays below 8 because HIGH/LOW gate paths remain 24.148/26.402 mm, VC remains 12.688 mm, the fan feed remains 81.922 mm and UART bottom remains 55.705 mm. The existing eFuse input network remains 43.806 mm, and 289.687 mm of inner1 signal routing remains.

The via count rises from 433 to 434, and trace objects rise from 633 to 636. This is a ground-corridor tradeoff rather than a via-count reduction. The score describes the complete board, including retained long routes and source/manufacturing constraints.

limitations: The 7.9 score is a subjective routing-quality judgment, not an arithmetic formula derived from length alone.
Planar economy excludes vertical barrels and counts overlapping trace objects separately; native finite-bound verification separately includes full 1.6 mm barrel transfer cost.
Copper continuity is reconstructed from captured traces, drilled pads/barrels and native BREP pours. It does not extract resistance, inductance, switching-loop response or thermal capacity.
Foreign-net clearance/shorts, current capacity, detailed ground-return support and source-plan architecture belong to separate final specialist reviews. A failure there overrides this routing score.
No dynamic, firmware, bench or manufacturing-release qualification is claimed. Supplier footprint mismatch warnings remain visible; their 24c/24d semantic content is preserved.
